subject: Private tenant maintenance: pin strategy, windows, and rollback roles
messages:
From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@fintegrate.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Maldonado <sofia.maldonado@acme-payments.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private tenant maintenance window & pin strategy

Hi Hannah,

We're planning a quarterly maintenance for our private deployment of Redwood in our VPC next month and want to align on two things:

1) Version pinning strategy — we run two clusters (prod and prod-canary). We need a recommended approach to pin model/runtime versions to avoid unexpected regressions. Is the team comfortable with pinning at build artifact + runtime env levels?

2) Maintenance windows — our ops folks proposed two candidate windows (weeknights local TZ): Aug 9 0200–0500 and Aug 12 2300–0200. Can Redwood operate a staged rollout with a canary (10% traffic) and a 30-minute observation before broad rollout?

Attached: acme_patch_manifest_v3.pdf (list of packages and CVEs), proposed_maint_windows.ics

We also have a quick security auditor question on rollback evidence — they want a short runbook we can show (pre/post checks, log preserves). Can you point us to that?

Thanks — Rajesh
Infrastructure Lead, Fintegrate
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@fintegrate.io>
Cc: Sofia Maldonado <sofia.maldonado@acme-payments.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private tenant maintenance window & pin strategy

Rajesh — thanks for the heads up and the manifest. Quick answers up front:

- Pinning: yes, we recommend a two-level pin: (1) model artifact SHA (immutable) and (2) runtime image tag pinned to a maintenance cohort (e.g., rwd-2028-07-cc1). That gives you deterministic inference behavior while allowing coordinated rollouts.

- Windows & rollout: we can do canary at 10% for 30 minutes, then 50% for 15 minutes, then 100% if metrics look green. We'll automate a traffic shift with an automatic rollback trigger on latency or error-rate thresholds.

- Runbook: attaching a short preflight checklist and a private_pin_matrix.csv that maps pin combinations we recommend. I'll loop Dev for the orchestration/playbook and Lauren for SLA/communication approvals.

Proposed next step — 30-min sync with your ops on Fri Jul 28 09:00 PT to finalize the exact steps and jumpseat for the day-of. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Hannah
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Private tenant maintenance window & pin strategy — internal runbook draft

Team — forwarding Rajesh's ask and the manifest. Below is a working runbook sketch for our internal ops play. Please review and call out gaps by EOD. I've flagged where we need owners.

1) Preflight (owner: Dev)
- Verify canary cluster (prod-canary) snapshot at t-30m; export KV/metadata backup 
- Run preflight smoke: 5 simple prompt traces, latency baseline, token accounting compare
- Verify log forwarding and retention (keep raw logs for +90 days per customer request)
- Confirm backup retention policy (S3 snapshot tagged with acme-prod-20280728)

2) Version pin strategy & mapping (owner: Marcus)
- Pin matrix included (private_pin_matrix.csv) maps exactly which model SHA + runtime image to push to canary
- If a hotfix is needed post-rollout, we will create a new image tag and patch only the affected nodes using rolling update with drain

3) Canary rollout plan (owner: Maya)
- Step 1: shift 10% traffic to canary for 30m, monitor: 95th latency, error rate, token cost delta, hallucination rate on eval set
- Step 2: if metrics OK, shift to 50% for 15m, then 100% for 15m; if any threshold breach, automated rollback to previous image and model SHA
- Cutover uses traffic-routing policy: region=us primary -> canary by affinity header for 10% sample

4) Rollback & evidence (owner: Lauren)
- Rollback executed automatically on threshold or manually via routing policy revert; capture snapshot, annotate ticket with time and reason
- Evidence bundle: preflight checks, post-rollback metrics, preserved logs link, CVE mitigation notes (checked against acme_patch_manifest_v3.pdf)

5) Communication & approvals (owner: Hannah)
- Day-of: #acme-maint Slack channel active; 3-way call (Redwood ops, Acme infra, Fintegrate)
- Post-maint completion note: include runbook outcomes, any incidents, and evidence bundle link

Open questions / risk notes:
- Network changes required for some CVE mitigations (see manifest) may need firewall rule updates from Acme infra. We need confirmation from Sofia if change windows overlap with our schedule.
- DBA: any DB migrations? Rajesh indicated none, but ask again.

Attachments: preflight-checklist.md, private_pin_matrix.csv

Please reply with any objections or owner changes. If silent, I'll treat these owners as confirmed and lock the Fri 09:00 sync with Acme.

—Hannah
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Private tenant maintenance window & pin strategy — internal runbook draft

LGTM on owners and the rollback thresholds. A couple of additions from infra side:

- I'll add an automated KV cache checkpoint step before canary shift (script: kv_checkpoint.sh)
- We should pre-warm the canary nodes with a small batch of synthetic traces 10m prior to shift to avoid cold-token latency artifacts
- Preflight smoke will also include a quick sanity check on KMS access (we've seen transient denies during prior rollouts)

I'll push an updated preflight-checklist.md to the Drive folder and put the runbook into the OPS page. Confirming I'm available for the Fri sync and for the day-of run.

—Dev
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
